  • the sephirot (divine attributes) have 3 axes, which 3D reality reflects

What is your view on baptisms for the dead, as mentioned in 1 Corinthians 15:29?

Aww man, I suppose you know you're asking me to argue against the LDS minority opinion specifically here...

I see Saul as a Pharisaical Jew using the epistles to render authoritative halachic rulings (which largely accord with the Gemara), and not just "a little Jewish" but one who had "ascended and descended in peace" [2 Cor. 12:2], one who still continued to bring the sacrifices after he accepted Jesus [Acts 21:26], one who was accused by false witnesses that he preached abrogation of the Torah [Acts 6:13]. Baptism for the dead has never existed in Pharisaical Judaism, and if Saul was changing his mind about the wisdom of changing the Torah I don't think he would do it with an offhand remark. 1 Cor. 15 is a long repudiation of heretics in the church at Corinth, Eleusinian in origin, which preached against resurrection of the dead but paradoxically were known for baptizing for the dead, which proves their intellectual inconsistency. That's why the wording is "they are baptized for the dead"; not "we" or "you", as is found throughout Corinthians to refer to the Church. I would even go so far as to say Saul here is prophetically foreshadowing the sects of Marcionists that will absorb these heretics in the future.
